Learning a language opens a new world.

Egyptian teacher Alaa Mamdouh Akef began learning Chinese at Cairo University in twenty oh four. His teacher gave him the Chinese name Gao Shan. He had been curious about Chinese writing and the people who used it since he was a child.

Learning the language helped him discover Chinese books. His first Chinese novel was a long story about the Three Kingdoms. He read it slowly, word by word, and needed six months to finish. Books made him want to experience China himself.

He arrived in Beijing in twenty twelve for further study. Today, he teaches Arabic at Peking University. He encourages students to learn about customs and ways of thinking as well as words. His experience shows how language learning can build understanding in both directions between cultures.
